name: PA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+15 partisan lean combined with a favorable national environment
Overwhelming fundraising edge for Scanlon ($1.26M raised vs. $21K for Manganaro)
Incumbent renominated with no outside spending against her
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 98%
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's strong Democratic lean, Scanlon's incumbency and roughly 60-to-1 fundraising advantage, no opposition outside spending, and markets pricing her near-certain re-election. With no polls or ratings suggesting vulnerability, the only real question is the size of her margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Scanlon or a sharp national shift toward Republicans could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon (D) is running.

overview:
Pennsylvania's 5th District leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Mary Gay Scanlon is seeking another term after being renominated. Her campaign has raised about $1.26 million and holds roughly $460,000 on hand, while Republican Nicholas Manganaro has raised about $21,000 with little cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and prediction markets put her chances near 98 percent.

No public polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and market pricing, all of which point the same way. The district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and the absence of serious opposition spending make a competitive contest unlikely. The main uncertainty is the size of the margin rather than the outcome, with the Republican needing a dramatic shift in the political environment to put the seat in play.
